Taking every 0 and only the last 1 gives value 1 with length 6.

title: Count Substrings With All Vowels and K Consonants
description:
You are given a string `word` of lowercase English letters and an integer k. A substring is counted when it contains each of the five vowels 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o' and 'u' at least once and contains exactly k consonants (letters that are not vowels). Return the number of counted substrings.

Example: word = "aeiouxyz" and k = 3. The only substring that contains all five vowels and exactly three consonants is the whole word "aeiouxyz" (index 0 to index 7). Every other substring misses a vowel or has a different number of consonants, so the answer is 1.
constraints: word consists only of lowercase English letters.
hints: Use a sliding window or a nested loop. For each start index, extend the end while counting vowels seen and consonants; count a substring when all five vowels are present and the consonant count is exactly k.

test_cases.explanation: The letter u is missing, so no substring has all five vowels.
The only substring with all five vowels and zero consonants is the whole word.

title: Maximum Number of Occurrences of a Substring
description:
Given a string `s` and three integers maxLetters, minSize and maxSize, find the substring with the most occurrences in s that satisfies two rules: it has at most maxLetters distinct letters, and its length is between minSize and maxSize (inclusive). Occurrences may overlap. Return the largest number of occurrences of such a substring (or 0 if there are none).

Example: s = "aababcaab", maxLetters = 2, minSize = 3, maxSize = 4. The substring "aab" occurs twice and has 2 distinct letters, so the answer is 2.
hints: A shorter substring can never occur less often than a longer one that contains it, so it is enough to check substrings of length minSize.

test_cases.explanation: "aab" appears twice with 2 distinct letters.
"aaa" appears twice (overlapping).

title: Number of Substrings With Only 1s
description:
Given a binary string `s`, count the substrings that contain only the character '1'. Each occurrence counts separately. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.

Example: s = "0110111". The block "11" gives 3 substrings ("1", "1", "11") and the block "111" gives 6 ("1" three times, "11" twice, "111" once). The total is 9.
hints: For each block of L consecutive 1s, it contributes L * (L + 1) / 2 substrings. Adding one character at a time, the count of new substrings ending at that character equals the current run length.

test_cases.explanation: Blocks of length 2 and 3 give 3 + 6 = 9 substrings.
Two blocks of length 1 give 1 + 1 = 2.

title: Maximum Product of Two Digits
description:
You are given an array `nums` of single digits (each value from 0 to 9). Choose two different positions in the array and multiply their values. Return the largest product you can make this way.

Example: nums = [3, 4, 5, 2, 7, 8]. The two largest digits are 8 and 7, and 8 * 7 = 56, which is the best product.
hints: The largest product of two values comes from the two largest values. Sort or track the top two.

test_cases.explanation: 8 * 7 = 56 is the best product.
Two 9s at different positions give 81.

title: Count the Number of Complete Components
description:
You are given an undirected graph with n vertices labeled 0 to n - 1 and a list of edges. A connected component is complete if every pair of its vertices is connected by an edge. Return the number of complete connected components. There are no duplicate edges and no self-loops.

Example: n = 6 and edges = [[0, 1], [0, 2], [1, 2], [3, 4]]. The component {0, 1, 2} is complete (all three pairs are connected). The component {3, 4} is complete. Vertex 5 alone is also a complete component. The answer is 3.
constraints: No duplicate edges and no self-loops.
hints: Group vertices into connected components with a union-find or DFS. A component with v vertices is complete when it has exactly v * (v - 1) / 2 edges.

test_cases.explanation: Components {0,1,2}, {3,4} and {5} are all complete.
The component {3, 4, 5} has only 2 edges for 3 vertices, so it is not complete.
All six pairs of the four vertices are joined, so the single component is complete.

title: Count Pairs of Similar Strings
description:
Two strings are similar if they contain exactly the same set of letters, regardless of how many times each letter appears or in what order. You are given an array `words`. Count the pairs (i, j) with i < j such that words[i] and words[j] are similar.

Example: words = ["aba", "aabb", "abcd", "bac", "aabc"]. Only the pairs ("aba", "aabb") and ("bac", "aabc") match, so the answer is 2.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Convert each word to the set of its letters. Two words are similar exactly when their sets are equal, so count equal sets.

test_cases.explanation: Two pairs match: ("aba", "aabb") share {a, b}, and ("bac", "aabc") share {a, b, c}.
All three words use exactly the letters a and b.
